digest.component_or_area: Cascade table and parent-child lifecycle state management (transition.py, concurrency.md)
propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table's one-eligible-status-per-edge shape guarantees only same-edge cascades, not a total parent-child ordering that prevents all child-ahead-of-parent states.
A closed child reactivating to in_progress under an open parent does not cascade and is documented-intended; only a closed parent is eligible on that edge.

A blocked child resuming to in_progress under an open parent does not cascade, despite the start-work gate firing on that edge; the gate and cascade answer different questions (work starting vs same-edge eligible ancestor).

The store enforces the operator-ruled invariant 'no non-terminal-state ticket is ever a child of a closed ticket' jointly via the table's two closed-source rows and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py, not via a predicate-based ordering.
The §I4a headline and _CASCADING_EDGES/transition.py docstrings must be narrowed to state the per-edge guarantee and the ruled invariant, while documenting both residuals as accepted behaviour.
